properties.rad_basis: TENORM — Final Engineering Report (April 2014) section 5.10 and Table 5.10; 608 cubic yards retained on site beneath the cover. ⛔ THE ORIGIN OF THIS SLAG IS CONTESTED WITHIN THE SITE'S OWN FILE. The 2012 OU1 ROD Amendment (p13) reports that during work on the adjacent Norampac facility "elevated levels of radiation was detected in slag fill used on the site. The slag, that is believed to have been generated at the former ELECTROMET facility, was used as fill in NUMEROUS LOCATIONS AROUND THE NIAGARA FALLS AREA." The 2013 Final Remedial Design (p425) instead calls it TENORM "associated with historic production of PHOSPHORUS SLAG ... reportedly derived from the processing of phosphorus ores from the Western New York area". Electromet made ferroalloys and separated niobium from columbite; phosphorus slag is a different industry and a TENORM source in its own right. Neither account is adopted here. Which is right decides whether radioactive slag fill across this city traces to Union Carbide (see C932143, 932042) or to a phosphorus producer. Sources: ROD.HW.932110.2012-03-28.OU1_ROD_AMENDMENT.pdf p13; Report.HW.932110.2013-02-25.Final_Remedial_Design_Re p425. Verified radionuclide detections in this site’s own documents: Radium / Radon, Thorium, Uranium (e.g. Report.HW.932110.2014-05-01.FER_and_SMP (page 92)).

properties.rad_basis: TENORM — GAMMA SCREENING, NOT YET CONFIRMED BY LABORATORY. NYSDEC-approved Remedial Investigation Work Plan (Mar 2026) required a screening survey under DMM-5, "Management of Soils Contaminated with Technically Enhanced Naturally Occurring Radioactive Materials". MJW GPS gamma walkover (Ludlum 3000 / 44-10 NaI), 30 April - 1 May 2026, Phase 1 outdoor areas only: 12,136 data points against a 2,362-point Hyde Park background mean of 7,732 CPM. 69 points exceeded the 1.5x criterion (11,598 CPM). The primary cluster of 52 points, immediately north of the former coal storage silo, ran 11,600-29,500 CPM (~1.5x-3.8x background) with 14 points above 3x. Soil sampling for Ra-226 was PENDING at the report date and Phase 2 (inside the structures) awaits demolition. The same ground carries the 2010 Phase I ESA recognised environmental condition "Former Coal Storage Pile and Unknown Historical Disposal of Fly Ash" and the pre-remediation lead maximum of 90,100 mg/kg. Source: Gamma Walkover Survey Report, MJW Doc. 26.1015.5, 26 May 2026, pp2-4.

properties.rad_basis: TENORM — GAMMA SCREENING, NOT YET CONFIRMED BY LABORATORY. NYSDEC-approved Remedial Investigation Work Plan (Mar 2026) required a screening survey under DMM-5, "Management of Soils Contaminated with Technically Enhanced Naturally Occurring Radioactive Materials". MJW GPS gamma walkover (Ludlum 3000 / 44-10 NaI), 30 April - 1 May 2026, Phase 1 outdoor areas only: 12,136 data points against a 2,362-point Hyde Park background mean of 7,732 CPM. 69 points exceeded the 1.5x criterion (11,598 CPM). The primary cluster of 52 points, immediately north of the former coal storage silo, ran 11,600-29,500 CPM (~1.5x-3.8x background) with 14 points above 3x. MJW conclusion: the scans "indicated the presence of elevated material on-site and potential TENORM material", and "additional screening and sampling is required to accurately characterize the material". Soil sampling for Ra-226 was PENDING at the report date and Phase 2 (inside the structures) awaits demolition. The same ground carries the 2010 Phase I ESA recognised environmental condition "Former Coal Storage Pile and Unknown Historical Disposal of Fly Ash" and the pre-remediation lead maximum of 90,100 mg/kg. Source: Gamma Walkover Survey Report, MJW Doc. 26.1015.5, 26 May 2026, pp2-4.

properties.rad_basis: Hand-validated radionuclide detections against Report.BCP.C932162.2014-11-15.FinalFER-AppendicesA-F: Radium / Radon, Thorium, Uranium, Actinium-228, Bismuth-212, Bismuth-214, Lead-212, Lead-214, Potassium-40, Thallium-208. The site's Final Engineering Report (15 Nov 2014) also records "Low-Level Radioactive Waste (LLRW)" — its term — encountered on 18 April 2014 during excavation of a storm-sewer trench in the northern portion of the mall building pad. It was found because A TRUCKLOAD TRIGGERED AN ELEVATED RADIATION WARNING AT THE RECEIVING LANDFILL, not by prior survey. Greater Radiological Dimensions (GRD) screened all subsequent excavation and ran two dose assessments; the simplistic maximum was 91 mRem/year against the NYSDEC/NYSDOH limit of 100 mRem/year, with a RESRAD model in Appendix T. NYSDEC approved an LLRW Work Plan on 1 May 2014 and authorised work to continue. A total of 258.53 tons in 11 loads was transported by 6NYCRR Part 364-permitted haulers to the Waste Management Mahoning Landfill, Mahoning, Ohio, on 20 June 2014. No isotope is named in the report. ⭐ ORIGIN: GRD's LLRW Work Plan states "The origin of this material is believed to be the backfill that was utilized during the construction of the existing shopping center" — it arrived as IMPORTED FILL, source unnamed. The slag read 35,000-52,000 CPM in the excavation and 65,000 CPM at the surface of a truck load, against a 5,000-7,000 CPM background. ⚠ Before the stop-work order, about 100 cubic yards of material from beside the find had already been moved to the southern part of the site and graded into a swale; GRD screened it at background and it was left in place. ⚠ CONTRADICTION WITH THE PRE-REMEDIAL ASSESSMENT: the 2013 Alternatives Analysis reported that "A Ludlum Geiger counter confirmed that the slag did not exhibit radioactivity" — the 2014 excavation found otherwise. Title records show the former Sabre Park parcel was owned by UNION CARBIDE CORPORATION, whose Metals Division (C932143) is the recorded generator of radioactive ferroalloy slag in this city; that connection is NOT stated in any document and is an open lead, not a finding. Sources: Report.BCP.C932162.2014-11-15.FinalFER-Text.pdf pp12, 26, 32-34, 38; FinalFER-AppendicesA-F.pdf p144; Report.BCP.C932162.2013-10-09.AlternativeAnalysisR pp16-17; Table 2 (p22 of the Tables volume). properties.rad_basis: TENORM recorded explicitly in the NYSDEC site record. ⭐ THE SITE ALSO HOLDS AN UNLOCATED BURIAL. Electromet (from 1896; Union Carbide Metals Division from 1975) processed uranium under Manhattan Engineer District / AEC contracts, then processed uranium and thorium commercially under New York State radioactive material licence 950-0139. From August 1965 to April 1972 it produced 505 tons of slag bearing 9,212 lb of thorium dioxide and 1,293 lb of uranium oxide ("yellow cake"); the slag was drummed in 55-gallon drums and buried on plant property in a hole 20 ft deep under 4-5 ft of soil. ⛔ The site's own Brownfield Cleanup Program file states: "The exact location of the disposal site has not been determined. Evidence that the waste has been recovered is absent. It is uncertain whether the area referred to is on the Royal Ave Union Carbide properties, or the 47th Street Praxair parcel." The MED/AEC work itself took place in the Area Plant, a building demolished in 1957, about 400 ft east of 47th Street and 400 ft south of Royal Avenue.
